schema_note: Classification only. Nothing here deletes or moves a lab; archive-candidate marks a lab whose migration shape needs an explicit decision.

criteria.golden: Declares assertions before execution in golden/manifest.template.json, separates execution status from hypothesis status, and classifies any pre-Golden artifacts.
criteria.migration-needed: Has runnable assets but no declared contract, so its verify step decides its own outcome instead of emitting evidence an evaluator can re-derive.
criteria.archive-candidate: Structure does not map onto the Golden run layout without a deliberate decision about how it should be split.

labs.reason: Has trigger.sh, verify.sh and cleanup.sh but no declared assertions. verify.sh decides its own outcome rather than emitting evidence for an evaluator.
Has trigger.sh and fix.sh but no verify.sh at all, so there is currently nothing to evaluate. Needs a collector plus a declared contract.

Ships a Golden contract: a manifest template declaring the discriminating assertion that separates SNAT exhaustion from destination failure, an evidence-classification naming what its retained captures cannot support, and a suite proving an unhealthy destination refuses the hypothesis. Both transports classify through one shared function, so a disagreement between urllib and requests can no longer look like evidence about Azure.

Structurally unlike every other lab: no top-level trigger/verify pair, instead three staged sub-labs (stage-0-config-discovery, lab-1-baseline-signature, lab-2-loopback-saturation). Migrating it means deciding whether each stage is its own Golden scenario. Archive-candidate is a decision to make that call deliberately, not a decision to delete.
